findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. On that alone they could describe it.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page's own proof of Athena's main promise (that you can trace a result to its models, cost and verdict) is broken. It shows an internal error message in the second section on the page, so a newcomer's first look at evidence is a failure.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Almost all of the page is a detailed study of another tool, firstmate, which a newcomer has probably never heard of. Someone who came to learn about Athena must scroll past states, transitions and 45 claims, and only gets an indirect sense of Athena's value from it.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections States of a piece of work, Transitions, Counters, Claims and sources

findings.text: The page does explain why the study exists. The bracketed claim ids that link to exact source lines show the traceability idea in concrete form.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project ... to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The next step is easy to find, because the header links to it. It gives the prerequisites, the clone and setup commands, and a sample `athena ask "add a changelog"` command, so a newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: This header link is meant for the project's owner, not a visitor. A newcomer won't know what the proposals are or whether the link concerns them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The Start here section and the "Words used first" list explain firstmate clearly. A reader who wants the study can follow it, including the plain-language walkthrough of one piece of work.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker"

findings.text: Several terms in the glossary are marked as undefined. This is honest, but it leaves gaps for a newcomer trying to follow the study.
findings.source: Glossary entries such as "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." and "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat."

findings.text: The closing section and the footer talk about how the page was built internally. They mean nothing to a first-time visitor and take space that a short summary of Athena could use.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
